newsitem.title: GERMANY: German dyke waters high but stable in Brandenburg.
newsitem.headline: German dyke waters high but stable in Brandenburg.

text.p: Germany's eastern state of Brandenburg could see crop and livestock losses if dykes and riverbanks weakened by heavy rainfall this month are unable to withstand pressure from further rains, a farm union (DBV) official said on Monday.
Emergency services this morning said dyke water levels were stable but serious, as rains let up temporarily.

If dykes burst -- which so far is not considered likely -- thousands of cows and pigs would be threatened and tens of thousands of hectares of crops could be devastated. Cattle could be led away but pigs and poultry would need to be transported.

"So far the rains have been a blessing after a drought in spring... farmers in this region are used to heavy summer rains and have no problem rearranging work schedules," the official said from the DBV base near Teltow southwest of Berlin.
"But if the dykes broke, there could be catastrophic damage not seen since the 1947 floods."
Water levels in Stuetzkow measured up to 9.12 metres against a 6.41 normal level.

The floods could last another two weeks, putting more pressure on banks and flood walls, which have been weakened by accumulated rain. Flooding of low-lying fields has necessitated some livestock evacuation.
Heavy rains have also led to lodging of grain, which may damage it permanently unless it recovers in sunny periods.
Barley and rye could need drying which would add to costs and operating costs would rise due to difficulties in working on the drenched soil.
Brandbenburg last year accounted for 2.5 million tonnes of grain out of Germany's 40 million tonne harvest.
Maize, grass and sugarbeet were more helped than damaged by the rains so far, but potato crops may develop mould, the DBV source said.
Floods have caused heavy damage and claimed lives in neighbouring Poland. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
